question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

We went to Bowbazaar in Kolkata to see the buildings for the lodging and accommodation of soldiers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. barracks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Barracks" means a building or group of buildings used for the lodging and accommodation of soldiers. (सैनिकों के रहने का स्थान / बैरक)

◦ Correct: We went to Bowbazaar in Kolkata to see the barracks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "paddocks" — small enclosed fields where horses are kept or exercised.

• Option 3 "hostels" — buildings providing inexpensive lodging, usually for students or travellers, not specifically soldiers.

• Option 4 "mints" — places where coins/currency are manufactured.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: cantonment (a military station/town), garrison (troops stationed to defend a place), arsenal (a store of weapons), armoury (a place where arms are kept).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The company decided / to phase up its / outdated technology / and embrace innovation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to phase up its.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "phase out", which means to gradually stop using or withdraw something. "Phase up" is not a standard phrasal verb; since the technology is "outdated", it must be discontinued, i.e., "phased out". (धीरे-धीरे समाप्त करना)

◦ Correct: The company decided to phase out its outdated technology and embrace innovation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The company decided", "outdated technology" and "and embrace innovation" are all grammatically correct segments.

• "Phase in" is the opposite phrasal verb — to gradually introduce something new.

NOTE

• Useful phrasal verbs for SSC: phase out (discontinue gradually), phase in (introduce gradually), do away with (abolish), wipe out (destroy completely).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Fabricate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Construct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fabricate" means to make, build or construct something; it can also mean to invent false information. Its closest synonym here is "construct" (to build or put together). (निर्माण करना / गढ़ना)

◦ Example: The workers fabricated/constructed the steel framework in a week.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Garments" (clothes) is a noun and unrelated.

• Option 3 "Fascinate" means to attract or charm greatly.

• Option 4 "Floral" (relating to flowers) is an adjective and unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fabricate: construct, manufacture, build, assemble; (in the sense of lying) invent, concoct, forge. Antonyms: demolish, destroy, dismantle.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Fantastic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Fanciful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fantastic" means imaginative, fanciful, strange or existing only in the imagination; informally it also means wonderful. Its closest synonym is "fanciful" (based on imagination rather than reality). (काल्पनिक / विलक्षण)

◦ Example: The novel is full of fantastic/fanciful creatures and imaginary lands.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Practical" (realistic, sensible) is nearly an antonym of fantastic.

• Option 3 "Graceful" (elegant in movement) and Option 4 "Delicate" (fragile, fine) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fantastic: fanciful, imaginary, fabulous, whimsical, unreal. Antonyms: real, practical, ordinary, realistic.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.

You must adhere to the rules of this place.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Comply.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adhere to" means to follow, obey or stick to (rules, beliefs or instructions). Its closest synonym is "comply (with)" — to act in accordance with rules or requests. (पालन करना)

◦ Example: All employees must adhere to/comply with the safety regulations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Strict" (severe) is an adjective, not a verb.

• Option 3 "Remember" (to recall) and Option 4 "Aware" (having knowledge) do not convey the sense of obeying rules.

NOTE

• Synonyms of adhere (to rules): comply, abide by, observe, obey, conform. Antonyms: violate, disobey, flout, breach. "Adhere" literally also means "to stick firmly" (like glue).

question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

After coming from a long journey he said, “It feels so _________ to be home”.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. good.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After verbs of sensation like "feel", we use an adjective in the positive degree when no comparison is being made. "It feels so good to be home" is the natural, correct expression. (अच्छा लगना)

◦ Correct: "It feels so good to be home."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "better" (comparative) and Option 4 "best" (superlative) are wrong because no comparison is intended, and "so" is followed by the positive degree.

• Option 3 "much good" is unidiomatic; "so much good" cannot qualify "feels" here.

NOTE

• Linking verbs (feel, seem, look, taste, smell, sound) are followed by adjectives, not adverbs: "It feels good", "She looks happy", "The soup tastes delicious".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A word, number, or other figure that looks the same when viewed (or rotated) upside down.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Ambigram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "ambigram" is a word, number or figure that reads the same (or as another word) when viewed or rotated upside down, e.g., the word "SWIMS" looks the same when turned upside down. (उलटा करने पर भी वैसा ही दिखने वाला शब्द/आकृति)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Anadiplosis" — a rhetorical device where the last word of one clause begins the next clause.

• Option 2 "Alliteration" — repetition of the same initial sound in nearby words (e.g., "she sells sea shells").

• Option 3 "Anagram" — a word formed by rearranging the letters of another word (e.g., "listen" → "silent").

NOTE

• Related terms: palindrome — a word/number that reads the same backwards and forwards (e.g., MADAM, 121); anagram — rearrangement of letters; ambigram — same when rotated/flipped.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

The sports teacher saw across the game and punished the students who were cheating in the game.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. through.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "see through" means to detect the true nature of something; to not be deceived by a trick. The teacher "saw through the game" — i.e., he detected the students' trick/deception. (चाल को भाँप लेना)

◦ Correct: The sports teacher saw through the game and punished the students who were cheating.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "See across", "see underneath", "see beside" and "see beneath" are not idiomatic in the sense of detecting deception.

• "Game" here figuratively means a trick or secret plan.

NOTE

• Useful "see" phrasal verbs: see through (detect a trick / support till the end), see off (bid farewell), see to (attend to), see about (deal with).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Squadroun.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Squadroun" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "squadron", meaning a unit of an air force, army cavalry or naval fleet. (स्क्वाड्रन — वायु सेना/सेना की टुकड़ी)

• Spelling key: SQUAD + RON (no "u" before the final "n").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Vigilante" (a person who takes the law into his own hands), "masquerade" (a false show; a masked ball) and "caricature" (a comically exaggerated portrait) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Commonly confused military words: squadron (air force unit), battalion (army unit), regiment, platoon. Watch the double letters and silent vowels in such words.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Piquant
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Bland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Piquant" means having a pleasantly sharp, spicy or stimulating taste/flavour. Its antonym is "bland", meaning tasteless, mild or lacking flavour. (चटपटा का विलोम — फीका)

◦ Example: The piquant chutney was served with rather bland rice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Bitter" is itself a strong taste, not the opposite of "sharp/spicy".

• Options 3 "Delicious" and 4 "Delectable" (both meaning very tasty) are closer to synonyms in spirit, not antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of piquant: spicy, tangy, zesty, pungent, savoury. Antonyms: bland, insipid, flavourless, tasteless.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Choronology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Choronology" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "chronology", meaning the arrangement of events in the order in which they occurred. (कालक्रम)

• Spelling key: CHRONO (time) + LOGY (study) — from Greek "chronos" = time; there is no "o" between "ch" and "r".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Competent" (capable), "soliloquy" (speaking one's thoughts aloud when alone, as in drama) and "protein" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words from "chronos" (time): chronology, chronic, chronicle, synchronise, anachronism. Note "protein" follows the exception to "i before e except after c".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in the usage of indefinite articles.

We have invited / our friends / for a / dinner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. for a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Names of meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner, supper) do not take an article when used in a general sense. So "invited our friends for dinner" is correct — the indefinite article "a" must be removed. (भोजन के नामों से पहले article नहीं लगता)

◦ Correct: We have invited our friends for dinner.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "We have invited", "our friends" and "dinner" are correct segments.

• An article is used with a meal only when it is qualified by an adjective: "a delicious dinner", "a grand lunch".

NOTE

• Article rules with meals: "have breakfast/lunch/dinner" (no article), but "a hearty breakfast", "the dinner hosted by the President" (specific).

question:
Select the idiom that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the given sentence meaningfully.

The negotiations reached a point where both parties had to (confront the consequences of their actions) and make tough decisions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. face the music.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "face the music" means to confront the unpleasant consequences of one's actions; to accept criticism or punishment. (अपने कर्मों के परिणाम भुगतना)

◦ Correct: ... both parties had to face the music and make tough decisions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "break a leg" — good luck (said before a performance).

• Option 3 "cut corners" — to do something cheaply or carelessly, skipping steps.

• Option 4 "get cold feet" — to become nervous and back out at the last moment.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "pay the piper", "reap what you sow", "take it on the chin" — all involve accepting consequences.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Mohan is still confused about his higher studies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Mohan is still confused about his higher studies." is grammatically correct — subject (Mohan) + verb (is) + adverb (still) + adjective (confused) + preposition (about) + object (his higher studies).

• "Confused about" is the correct adjective + preposition combination.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Mohan is still" — correct placement of the adverb "still" between the auxiliary and the adjective.

• "his higher studies" — correct possessive usage; "higher studies" is a standard expression for advanced education.

NOTE

• Common adjective + preposition pairs: confused about, good at, afraid of, interested in, satisfied with, responsible for. Errors in such pairs are frequently tested in SSC exams.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Postuer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Postuer" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "posture", meaning the position in which a person holds his body while standing or sitting. (शारीरिक मुद्रा)

• Spelling key: POS + TURE — it ends in "-ture" like the other options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Gesture" (a movement of the hand/head to express an idea), "culture" (customs and way of life) and "lecture" (an educational talk) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-ture": posture, gesture, culture, lecture, nature, picture, capture, mixture, furniture. The "-ture" ending is pronounced /chər/.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

My old car was pressed into service as an emergency vehicle for my ailing grandmother.
option_3: To use for a particular purpose when a special need occurs.
option_4: Used to take someone to the hospital
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. To use for a particular purpose when a special need occurs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "pressed into service" means to be made to serve or be used for a purpose, usually in an emergency or when a special need arises. (आवश्यकता पड़ने पर काम में लाना)

◦ In the sentence, the old car was used in an emergency to help the ailing grandmother.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 describe literal or narrow situations, not the general idiomatic meaning of using something because of a sudden need.

NOTE

• Related expressions: "call into service", "bring into play", "make do with" (use whatever is available). "Press" here means to force into use.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Ramya would gladly help Manya if you had asked her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. would have gladly helped.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The if-clause "if you had asked her" is in the past perfect, so the sentence is a third conditional (unreal past). The main clause must take "would have + past participle (V3)" — "would have gladly helped". (तृतीय conditional)

◦ Correct: Ramya would have gladly helped Manya if you had asked her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "is to gladly help" and Option 2 "will gladly help" refer to present/future and clash with "had asked".

• Option 3 "was to have gladly helped" is not the standard conditional structure.

NOTE

• Conditional patterns: First — If + present, will + V1; Second — If + past, would + V1; Third — If + past perfect, would have + V3 (for imagined past situations).

question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
option_1: The hard disc of a computer on a desk needs to be repaired at the earliest.
option_2: A hard disc of the computer on the desk needs to be repaired at the earliest.
option_3: The hard disc of the computer on the desk needs to be repaired at the earliest.
option_4: The hard disc of a computer on the desk needs to be repaired at an earliest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The hard disc of the computer on the desk needs to be repaired at the earliest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• We are speaking of a specific hard disc of a specific computer on a specific desk, so the definite article "the" is required before all three nouns: "The hard disc of the computer on the desk".

• The fixed phrase is "at the earliest" (as soon as possible), never "at an earliest".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses "a computer on a desk" (indefinite) though a particular computer is meant.

• Option 2 wrongly uses "A hard disc" for the specific disc.

• Option 4 wrongly says "at an earliest".

NOTE

• "The" is used for things already identified or made specific by a phrase like "of the computer/on the desk". Superlatives also take "the": at the earliest, at the latest, the best.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Gregarious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sociable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gregarious" means fond of company; enjoying being with other people; sociable. (मिलनसार)

◦ Example: A gregarious/sociable person makes friends easily at parties.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Isolated" (alone, separated), Option 3 "Introverted" (inward-looking, shy) and Option 4 "Reserved" (not revealing feelings, quiet) are all antonyms of gregarious.

• "Gregarious" is also used of animals that live in flocks or herds.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gregarious: sociable, outgoing, extroverted, affable, convivial. Antonyms: introverted, reserved, unsociable, reclusive.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The manager had / thrown up the / drunk people sitting / inside his office premises.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. thrown up the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "throw out", meaning to expel or force someone to leave a place. "Throw up" means to vomit, which is absurd here. So it should be "had thrown out the drunk people". (बाहर निकालना)

◦ Correct: The manager had thrown out the drunk people sitting inside his office premises.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The manager had", "drunk people sitting" and "inside his office premises" are grammatically acceptable segments.

NOTE

• "Throw" phrasal verbs: throw out (expel/discard), throw up (vomit / produce hastily), throw away (discard), throw off (get rid of), throw in (add free of cost).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. descended.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Descended from" means to have developed or evolved from an ancestor. The passage says man has evolved "descended from arboreal apes" (apes that live in trees). (वंशज होना)

◦ Correct: Man, it would seem, has descended from arboreal apes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "ascended" (climbed up), Option 3 "recommended" (suggested) and Option 4 "extended" (stretched) do not collocate with "from ... apes" in the sense of ancestry.

• "Arboreal" means living in trees (वृक्षवासी).

NOTE

• "Be descended from" is the fixed expression for lineage/evolution: "Birds are descended from dinosaurs." The noun is "descendant"; the antonym concept is "ancestor".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. perpetually.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Perpetually" means constantly; all the time; without interruption. The apes were "perpetually occupied in gymnastics" — always busy swinging and climbing. (निरंतर / सदा)

◦ Correct: They were perpetually occupied in gymnastics ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "professionally" (as a profession) does not suit apes.

• Option 3 "bisectionally" is not a standard English word in this context.

• Option 4 "conspiratorially" (in a secretive, plotting manner) does not fit "occupied in gymnastics".

NOTE

• Synonyms of perpetually: constantly, continually, incessantly, eternally. The adjective is "perpetual" (a perpetual motion machine, perpetual snow).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. agility.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Agility" means the ability to move quickly, easily and nimbly. Constant gymnastics would naturally give the apes "an agility which to us is truly astonishing". (फुर्ती)

◦ Correct: They were perpetually occupied in gymnastics and acquired an agility ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "civility" (politeness), Option 2 "density" (compactness) and Option 4 "variability" (tendency to change) cannot be acquired through gymnastics.

• Note the article "an" before the blank — it correctly precedes the vowel sound of "agility".

NOTE

• Synonyms of agility: nimbleness, quickness, dexterity, suppleness. The adjective is "agile" (an agile gymnast, an agile mind).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. astonishing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Astonishing" means very surprising; amazing. The agility of the apes, when compared with human ability, is "truly astonishing" to us. (आश्चर्यजनक)

◦ Correct: ... acquired an agility which to us is truly astonishing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "disappointing" (causing dissatisfaction), Option 2 "boring" (dull) and Option 4 "frightening" (causing fear) do not express admiration for remarkable agility.

NOTE

• Synonyms of astonishing: amazing, astounding, stunning, staggering, remarkable. The passage is adapted from Bertrand Russell's humorous prose on human evolution.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. adequate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adequate" means enough; sufficient for the need. As the apes' numbers increased, the supply of coconuts was "no longer adequate" — i.e., no longer enough for all of them. (पर्याप्त)

◦ Correct: ... their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer adequate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "deficient" (insufficient) would create a double negative with "no longer" and reverse the intended meaning.

• Option 2 "delicate" (fragile) and Option 4 "consecrate" (to declare sacred — a verb) do not fit.

NOTE

• Synonyms of adequate: sufficient, enough, satisfactory, ample. Antonyms: inadequate, deficient, insufficient, scanty. Watch out for "no longer + adjective" constructions — the adjective itself must be positive in sense.

question: Which state in India has the highest population density as per the 2011 census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, Bihar has the highest population density among Indian states — about 1,106 persons per square kilometre. (बिहार — सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या घनत्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• West Bengal (about 1,028 persons/sq km) comes second and Kerala third among states.

• Among Union Territories, Delhi (NCT) has the highest density (about 11,320 persons/sq km).

• The lowest density state is Arunachal Pradesh (17 persons/sq km).

NOTE

• Population density = total population ÷ area. India's average density in 2011 was 382 persons/sq km. Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state, but Bihar is the most densely populated.

question: Who among the following started the Khilafat Movement against the British government?
option_3: Syed Raza Ali and Muhammad Ali Jinnah
option_4: Maulana Mazharul Haque and Mian Abdul Aziz
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Khilafat Movement (1919–1924) was started by the Ali brothers — Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali — against the British government's treatment of the Ottoman Caliph (Khalifa) of Turkey after World War I. (ख़िलाफ़त आंदोलन — अली बंधु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other leaders associated with it were Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Hakim Ajmal Khan and Hasrat Mohani.

• Mahatma Gandhi supported the Khilafat Movement and merged it with the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22) to build Hindu–Muslim unity.

• The movement lost relevance when Mustafa Kemal Ataturk abolished the Caliphate in Turkey in 1924.

NOTE

• The All India Khilafat Committee was formed in 1919; a Khilafat Day was observed on 17 October 1919.

question: Which of the following country's official language is Sinhala?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sri Lanka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sinhala (Sinhalese) is an official language of Sri Lanka, along with Tamil. It is spoken by the majority Sinhalese community. (सिंहली — श्रीलंका)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sri Lanka — capitals: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte (administrative/legislative) and Colombo (commercial); currency: Sri Lankan Rupee.

• Official languages of the other options: Maldives — Dhivehi; Myanmar — Burmese; Nepal — Nepali.

NOTE

• Sri Lanka is separated from India by the Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar; it was formerly called Ceylon.

question: Who among the following Dance Gurus got Padma Vibhushan in the year 2000?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, the legendary Odissi dance guru, received the Padma Vibhushan in 2000. He was the first person from Odisha to receive this honour and is credited with reviving and popularising Odissi. (केलुचरण महापात्र — ओडिसी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Odissi is the classical dance form of Odisha, known for its "tribhangi" (three-bend) posture.

• Birju Maharaj was the doyen of Kathak (he received the Padma Vibhushan in 1986); Bipin Singh was a Manipuri dance guru; Ileana Citaristi is an Italian-born Odissi dancer (Padma Shri, 2006).

NOTE

• The Padma Vibhushan is India's second-highest civilian award, after the Bharat Ratna, followed by the Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.

question: Who among the following authors wrote 'Kamayani', 'Dhruvswamini', 'Kankal', 'Titli', 'Skandagupta', 'Lahar' and 'Mamta'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaishankar Prasad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jaishankar Prasad (1889–1937), one of the greatest Hindi writers, wrote the epic poem "Kamayani", the plays "Dhruvswamini" and "Skandagupta", the novels "Kankal" and "Titli", and the works "Lahar" and "Mamta". (जयशंकर प्रसाद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jaishankar Prasad was one of the four pillars of the Chhayavad (Romantic) movement in Hindi literature, along with Suryakant Tripathi 'Nirala', Sumitranandan Pant and Mahadevi Verma.

• "Kamayani" (1936), based on Manu, Shraddha and Ida, is considered a masterpiece of modern Hindi poetry.

NOTE

• Bhisham Sahni wrote "Tamas"; Krishna Sobti wrote "Zindaginama" (Jnanpith awardee); Nirala wrote "Saroj Smriti" and "Ram ki Shakti Puja".

question: There shall be a/an ________ with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President in the exercise of his functions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Council of Ministers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 74(1) of the Constitution provides: "There shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President, who shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice." (मंत्रिपरिषद — अनुच्छेद 74)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• By the 42nd Amendment (1976), the advice of the Council of Ministers was made binding on the President; the 44th Amendment (1978) allowed the President to send it back once for reconsideration.

• Article 75 — the Prime Minister is appointed by the President; other ministers are appointed on the PM's advice; the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

NOTE

• The Attorney General (Article 76) is the highest law officer; the Council of States is the Rajya Sabha (Article 80); Parliament consists of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha (Article 79).

question: Which of the following statements is correct?
option_1: Chlorine has the highest electron affinity, while fluorine has the highest electronegativity.
option_2: Fluorine has the highest electron affinity, while chlorine has the highest electronegativity.
option_3: Fluorine has the highest electron affinity and the highest electronegativity.
option_4: Fluorine has the highest electron affinity, while bromine has the highest electronegativity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chlorine has the highest electron affinity, while fluorine has the highest electronegativity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chlorine (Cl) has the highest electron affinity (electron gain enthalpy) in the periodic table — higher than fluorine — because fluorine's very small size causes strong electron–electron repulsion in its compact 2p subshell when a new electron is added.

• Fluorine (F) is the most electronegative element (electronegativity = 4.0 on the Pauling scale). (क्लोरीन — सर्वाधिक इलेक्ट्रॉन बंधुता; फ्लोरीन — सर्वाधिक विद्युत ऋणात्मकता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Electron affinity — the energy released when an atom gains an electron; electronegativity — the tendency of an atom to attract shared electrons in a bond.

• Order of electron affinity in halogens: Cl > F > Br > I (fluorine is an exception due to its small size).

NOTE

• Halogens (Group 17): F, Cl, Br, I, At. Fluorine is also the most reactive non-metal; caesium/francium are the least electronegative elements.

question: In which game are terms like break, cannons, cue, potting, and kissed commonly used?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Billiards.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Terms like "break, cannons, cue, potting and kissed" are used in the game of Billiards (and the related cue sports snooker/pool). The game is played on a cloth-covered table with a cue stick and balls. (बिलियर्ड्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Famous Indian billiards/snooker players: Pankaj Advani (multiple-time World Billiards Champion, Padma Bhushan awardee), Geet Sethi and Michael Ferreira.

• Terms of other games — Golf: birdie, bogey, eagle, tee; Polo: chukker, mallet; Chess: checkmate, gambit, stalemate, castling.

NOTE

• Sports terms are frequently asked in SSC exams: Cricket — googly, LBW; Hockey — penalty corner, scoop; Football — dribble, offside; Badminton — smash, drop shot.

question: Who was sent as an envoy to China during the time of Muhammad bin Tughluq?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ibn Battuta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ibn Battuta, the famous Moroccan traveller, came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq, who appointed him Qazi (judge) of Delhi and later sent him as his envoy to China (to the Mongol Yuan court) in 1342. (इब्न बतूता — चीन में राजदूत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ibn Battuta's travel account, the "Rihla" (written in Arabic), is a valuable source for the history of the Delhi Sultanate.

• Ziauddin Barani wrote "Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi"; Al-Biruni (who came with Mahmud of Ghazni) wrote "Kitab-ul-Hind"; Hasan Nizami wrote "Taj-ul-Maasir".

NOTE

• Muhammad bin Tughluq (r. 1325–1351) is known for shifting the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and introducing token (copper/bronze) currency — both failed experiments.

question: Who has been appointed as the 'UPI Safety Ambassador' by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) to enhance safety awareness on digital payment platforms in November 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pankaj Tripathi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2023, the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) appointed actor Pankaj Tripathi as the "UPI Safety Ambassador" to spread awareness about safe digital payment practices through the 'UPI Safety Shield' campaign. (पंकज त्रिपाठी — यूपीआई सेफ्टी एंबेसडर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• NPCI (founded 2008) is the umbrella organisation for retail payments in India, set up by the RBI and IBA; it operates UPI, RuPay, IMPS, FASTag (NETC) and Bharat BillPay.

• UPI (Unified Payments Interface) was launched in 2016; BHIM is NPCI's UPI app.

NOTE

• UPI has expanded abroad — accepted in countries such as Singapore, UAE, France, Sri Lanka, Mauritius and Nepal/Bhutan — making digital-payment current affairs important for SSC exams.

question: Which Indian city hosted the Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy event in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ranchi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy 2023 was hosted by Ranchi (Jharkhand) at the Marang Gomke Jaipal Singh Munda Astroturf Hockey Stadium (27 October – 5 November 2023). (रांची — महिला एशियाई हॉकी चैंपियंस ट्रॉफी 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India won the title, defeating Japan 4–0 in the final — India's second Women's Asian Champions Trophy title (first in 2016).

• Savita Punia captained the Indian team.

NOTE

• Bhubaneswar–Rourkela hosted the Men's Hockey World Cup 2023; Hockey India's flagship venues include Kalinga Stadium (Bhubaneswar) and Birsa Munda Stadium (Rourkela — the largest hockey stadium in India).

question: Who is known to have revived Bharatnatyam dance form in its modern version today?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rukmini Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rukmini Devi Arundale is credited with reviving Bharatanatyam in its modern, respectable form. She removed elements considered objectionable, brought the dance out of the temple/devadasi tradition to the general stage, and founded Kalakshetra (1936) at Adyar, Chennai. (रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल — भरतनाट्यम का पुनरुद्धार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra.

• T. Balasaraswati was a legendary Bharatanatyam dancer of the traditional style; Yamini Krishnamurthy and Mallika Sarabhai are celebrated dancers of a later generation.

• Rukmini Devi was the first woman nominated to the Rajya Sabha (1952) and received the Padma Bhushan.

NOTE

• India's eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: Megasthenes was an ambassador who was sent to the court of which Indian ruler by the Greek ruler, Seleucus Nicator?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandragupta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator (Alexander's general) to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra. He wrote the famous account "Indica". (मेगस्थनीज — चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य का दरबार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire (321 BCE) with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra.

• After defeating Seleucus (c. 305 BCE), Chandragupta received territories including Kabul, Kandahar and Herat; in return Seleucus received 500 war elephants.

• Chandragupta later embraced Jainism and died at Shravanabelagola (Karnataka).

NOTE

• Greek envoys: Megasthenes — court of Chandragupta; Deimachus — court of Bindusara; Dionysius — court of Bindusara/Ashoka (sent by Ptolemy of Egypt).

question: Who among the following founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 with the help of MG Ranade?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Servants of India Society" was founded in 1905 at Pune by Gopal Krishna Gokhale, with the help of his mentor Mahadev Govind Ranade. Its aim was to train national missionaries for the service of India through education, social reform and upliftment of the poor. (गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले — सर्वेंट्स ऑफ इंडिया सोसाइटी, 1905)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gokhale was a leading Moderate leader of the Indian National Congress (President of the Banaras session, 1905) and is called the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.

• He was also a member of the Imperial Legislative Council and played a key role in the Morley–Minto reforms discussions.

NOTE

• Other organisations: Deccan Education Society (1884 — Tilak, Agarkar), Sabarmati Ashram (1917 — Gandhi), Home Rule Leagues (1916 — Tilak and Annie Besant).

question: On 25 August 2023, which State Government expanded its ongoing 'Breakfast Scheme' for students of classes 1 to 5, studying in 31,008 government schools across the State?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 25 August 2023, the Tamil Nadu government expanded its "Chief Minister's Breakfast Scheme" to cover students of classes 1 to 5 in 31,008 government schools across the state. (तमिलनाडु — मुख्यमंत्री नाश्ता योजना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme was originally launched on 15 September 2022 by Chief Minister M. K. Stalin; it provides free nutritious breakfast to government primary school children to fight hunger and improve attendance.

• Tamil Nadu has a pioneering legacy in school nutrition — the Mid-Day Meal Scheme was popularised by CM K. Kamaraj and expanded by M. G. Ramachandran.

NOTE

• The national Mid-Day Meal Scheme (1995) is now called PM POSHAN; such welfare-scheme questions are common in SSC current affairs.

question: Which chemical compound is commonly utilised as a preservative in tomato sauce?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium Benzoate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sodium benzoate (C₆H₅COONa)" is the chemical compound commonly used as a preservative in tomato sauce/ketchup, jams, squashes and pickles. It prevents the growth of bacteria, yeast and fungi in acidic foods. (सोडियम बेंजोएट — परिरक्षक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sodium benzoate is the sodium salt of benzoic acid; its food additive code is E211.

• Other common preservatives: potassium metabisulphite (fruit juices), acetic acid/vinegar (pickles), common salt and sugar (traditional preservation).

NOTE

• Preservatives work best in acidic media (pH < 4.5), which is why sodium benzoate suits tomato products. Class I preservatives — natural (salt, sugar, oil, vinegar); Class II — chemical (benzoates, sulphites, sorbates).

question: The Guindy National Park is located in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Guindy National Park is located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. It is one of the smallest national parks in India and among the very few situated inside a city. (गिंडी राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — चेन्नई, तमिलनाडु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It is home to blackbucks, spotted deer (chital), jackals and many bird, butterfly and reptile species; the Raj Bhavan and IIT Madras campuses adjoin it.

• Other protected areas of Tamil Nadu: Mudumalai National Park & Tiger Reserve, Anamalai (Indira Gandhi) National Park, Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park, Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary.

NOTE

• National parks inside/near metros: Guindy NP (Chennai) and Sanjay Gandhi (Borivali) NP (Mumbai) — a favourite SSC static-GK point.

question: In which Indian state do we find caves named after elephant statues found in it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Elephanta Caves" are located on Elephanta Island (Gharapuri) in Mumbai Harbour, Maharashtra. The Portuguese named the island "Elephanta" after a large stone elephant statue found on it. (एलिफेंटा गुफाएँ — महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The caves (c. 5th–8th century CE) are famous for rock-cut temples dedicated to Lord Shiva, especially the magnificent Trimurti (three-faced Shiva) sculpture.

• Elephanta Caves were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

• The original elephant statue is now kept in the Jijamata Udyaan (Byculla), Mumbai.

NOTE

• Famous cave groups of Maharashtra: Ajanta (Buddhist paintings), Ellora (Buddhist–Hindu–Jain; Kailasa temple) and Elephanta — all UNESCO sites.

question: Which country was a major importer of dye intermediates and castor oils from India in 2022-23?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2022-23, China was a major importer of dye intermediates and castor oil from India. India is the world's largest producer and exporter of castor oil, and China is its biggest buyer for industrial use. (चीन — डाई इंटरमीडिएट व अरंडी तेल का प्रमुख आयातक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Castor (arandi) is grown mainly in Gujarat and Rajasthan; Gujarat alone accounts for the bulk of India's production.

• Dye intermediates are chemicals used to manufacture dyes and pigments; Gujarat and Maharashtra are India's chemical-industry hubs.

• India–China trade is heavily tilted in China's favour overall, but these items are notable Indian exports to China.

NOTE

• India is the largest global exporter of castor oil, used in lubricants, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, paints and nylon manufacture.

question: The Krebs cycle of aerobic respiration is carried out within which of the following cell organelles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mitochondria.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle / TCA cycle) of aerobic respiration takes place in the matrix of the mitochondria. (क्रेब्स चक्र — माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Steps of aerobic respiration: Glycolysis (in the cytoplasm) → Krebs cycle (mitochondrial matrix) → Electron Transport Chain (inner mitochondrial membrane), producing about 36–38 ATP per glucose molecule.

• The mitochondrion is called the "powerhouse of the cell"; it has its own DNA and ribosomes.

• The Krebs cycle was discovered by Sir Hans Krebs (1937), who won the Nobel Prize in 1953.

NOTE

• "Spirogyra" is not an organelle at all — it is a filamentous green alga; lysosomes are "suicide bags" of the cell; the nucleus controls cell activities.

question: When the pH value of soils is more than 7.5, they are considered to be:
solution_text:
The correct answer is alkaline soils.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On the pH scale (0–14), a value of 7 is neutral, below 7 is acidic and above 7 is alkaline (basic). Hence soils with a pH above 7.5 are considered "alkaline soils". (क्षारीय मृदा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Alkaline/usar soils are common in dry regions of India (parts of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan); they are reclaimed by adding gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O).

• Acidic soils (pH < 7) are treated with lime (CaO/CaCO₃).

• The pH scale was introduced by the Danish chemist S. P. L. Sørensen (1909).

NOTE

• Most crops grow best in soils of pH 6.0–7.5. pH of common substances: lemon juice ~2, pure water 7, baking soda ~9, milk of magnesia ~10.

question: The cultural sport of Maharashtra, 'dahi-handi' is associated with which festival?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Krishna Janmashtami.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dahi-handi", the cultural sport of Maharashtra, is celebrated on the day after Krishna Janmashtami (the birth anniversary of Lord Krishna). Teams of "Govindas" form human pyramids to break an earthen pot (handi) filled with curd (dahi) hung at a height, recreating young Krishna's stealing of butter. (दही-हांडी — कृष्ण जन्माष्टमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Janmashtami falls on the Ashtami (8th day) of Krishna Paksha in the month of Bhadrapada.

• In 2022, Maharashtra accorded dahi-handi the status of an official sport, calling it "Pro Govinda".

NOTE

• Major Maharashtra festivals: Ganesh Chaturthi (public celebration started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1893), Gudi Padwa (Marathi New Year) and dahi-handi (Janmashtami).

question: Which of the following dance performances begins with the Kelikottu?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Kathakali" performance traditionally begins with the "Kelikottu" — the ceremonial beating of drums (chenda and maddalam) with cymbals to announce the performance and invite the audience. (केलिकोट्टु — कथकली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathakali is the classical dance-drama of Kerala, famous for its elaborate make-up (vesham), huge costumes and mudras; themes are drawn from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

• Traditional stages of a Kathakali recital: Kelikottu, Todayam, Purappadu, Melappadam, Kathi, etc.

• Famous exponents: Kalamandalam Gopi, Guru Kunchu Kurup, Kavungal Chathunni Panicker.

NOTE

• Kerala's dance forms: Kathakali (classical, male-dominated), Mohiniyattam (classical, feminine grace), Theyyam and Ottamthullal (ritual/folk).

question: The budget of the central government is known as the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is union budget.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The budget of the central government of India is known as the "Union Budget". The Constitution (Article 112) calls it the "Annual Financial Statement" — a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for a financial year. (केंद्रीय बजट — अनुच्छेद 112)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Union Budget is presented by the Union Finance Minister, normally on 1 February; since 2017 the Railway Budget stands merged with it.

• The word "budget" comes from the French "bougette" (small bag).

• The first budget of independent India was presented by R. K. Shanmukham Chetty (1947); Morarji Desai presented the most budgets.

NOTE

• State governments present their own "state budgets" under Article 202. A "revised budget/estimate" refers to mid-year revision of estimates, not the budget itself.

question: What writ means 'We Command'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mandamus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mandamus" is a Latin term meaning "We Command". This writ is issued by the Supreme Court (Article 32) or a High Court (Article 226) to a public official, body or lower court, commanding it to perform a public/legal duty that it has failed to perform. (परमादेश — 'हम आदेश देते हैं')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Habeas Corpus — "to have the body" — against illegal detention.

• Prohibition — issued by a higher court to a lower court to stop proceedings beyond its jurisdiction.

• Certiorari — "to be certified" — quashes an order already passed by a lower court/tribunal.

• Quo Warranto — "by what authority" — questions a person's claim to a public office.

NOTE

• Mandamus cannot be issued against the President or Governors, against private individuals, or to enforce a discretionary (non-mandatory) duty. The Supreme Court is the guarantor of Fundamental Rights under Article 32, which Dr Ambedkar called the "heart and soul" of the Constitution.
